text:
Mason Marchment is one of the veterans in a young San Jose lineup, and the box score is about what you'd want: 13 points in 28 games, five on the power play, where he now works the second unit beside Michael Misa. He's a big body (6'5", 34 hits) who still gets to the front of the net, with 7.1 expected goals so far.

The worry is what happens when he's out there at five on five. San Jose has only 42.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is negative. Some of that is the team around him, and some of it is bad luck: the Sharks have scored 6.2 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on, the kind of gap that usually closes.

Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards last season, mostly on even-strength offense, with his defensive impact in the 85th percentile. That version of Marchment hasn't shown up on defense yet. Watch his line's chance share over the next month; that's what decides whether he stays in the top nine.
